bibliographic.title: Compliance-Scored Best-of-N Guardrail Orchestration for Multimodal Document Generation in Payments Dispute Defense
bibliographic.citation_apa: Sundar, N. A., & Morabia, T. (2026). Compliance-Scored Best-of-N Guardrail Orchestration for Multimodal Document Generation in Payments Dispute Defense. eBay Inc.

methodology.method_family: Technical framework development with aggregate operational scenario evaluation and reviewer-calibrated Responsible-AI quality review
methodology.study_design: Non-randomized aggregate operational scenario readouts comparing variable cohorts versus controls; compliance-scored best-of-N guardrail orchestration evaluation
methodology.sample_description: Payments dispute defense document-generation operational cohorts (variable vs control); 770 generated-evidence reviews; 70-case OCR slice
methodology.sample_size: 301/659 vs 536/1548 for overall count win rates; 770 generated-evidence reviews; 70 OCR cases
methodology.technology_context: Multimodal LLM document generation with unified guardrail orchestration (PII detection, content moderation, schema constraints, domain rules), best-of-N candidate selection, early exit, and distributed-systems deployment

eligibility.decision_rationale: The paper provides strong operational evidence on compliance-scored guardrail orchestration, policy enforcement, human oversight, and Responsible-AI review in high-stakes regulated payments document generation. It does not address conversational systems, chatbots, agents, or conversational governance, so it is better classified as supporting rather than central evidence for a review focused on conversational governance.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only partial PDF text was provided; venue, peer-review status, full methods, and complete limitations require verification.

appraisal.notes: Objectives and contributions are clearly stated. The evaluation design is explicitly non-randomized at the aggregate scenario level, which limits causal inference despite reported confidence intervals and p-values. Reproducibility is partially documented via request interface, scoring logic, pseudocode, and operational evidence boundaries.

cerqual.explanation: Findings are coherent and operationally detailed for guardrail orchestration in payments dispute document generation, but the non-randomized design and partial text limit confidence. Relevance to the review is moderate because governance, compliance, guardrails, and human oversight are central to the paper, while conversational governance is absent.

coding.theme: Compliance-scored guardrail orchestration for regulated LLM document generation
coding.subtheme: Payments dispute defense and structured multimodal outputs

synthesis.main_claim: A unified, configuration-first guardrail orchestration layer using compliance-scored best-of-N selection improves policy-compliant multimodal document generation in payments dispute defense while reducing fragmented gate latency and operational rework.
synthesis.contribution: Introduces a distributed-systems guardrail framework that consolidates PII detection, moderation, schema checks, and domain rules; uses weighted compliance scoring for candidate selection and early exit; and reports production-style outcomes including 91% compliance within latency constraints plus cohort-level win-rate improvements and reviewer-calibrated Responsible-AI signals.
synthesis.limitations: Evaluation relies on aggregate operational scenario readouts rather than a randomized A/B test; some effect estimates are directionally positive but not statistically significant; transfer to other domains requires recalibration of rule weights, thresholds, risk routing, and human-review policies; Responsible-AI review identifies operational risks requiring human oversight.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence for operational guardrail orchestration, compliance scoring, policy enforcement, and human oversight in regulated LLM deployments. Do not use as central evidence for conversational governance, chatbot/agent interaction control, or dialogue-specific accountability mechanisms.

evidence.claim: Study focuses on high-stakes regulated enterprise document generation using LLMs with safety and compliance risks.
evidence.excerpt: High-stakes enterprise document generation (e.g., financial dispute narratives, compliance notices, audit summaries) demands schema correctness, policy compliance, and low-latency operation at scale.

evidence.claim: Paper presents a unified guardrail orchestration layer with compliance-scored best-of-N selection.
evidence.excerpt: We present a guardrail orchestration layer for text and image inputs that couples multi-candidate generation with an explicit compliance score used for early exit.

evidence.claim: Operational readout reports compliance and latency performance.
evidence.excerpt: The available operational readout reports 5 attempts within 20 s and 91 % compliance.

evidence.claim: Evaluation is non-randomized aggregate scenario comparison.
evidence.excerpt: For payments dispute defense summaries, we analyze aggregate operational scenario readouts rather than a randomized A/B test.

evidence.claim: Variable cohorts show higher win rates than controls overall.
evidence.excerpt: Variable cohorts show higher count win rates than controls overall (301/659 vs. 536/1548; +11.0 pp, 95% CI [6.6, 15.5], p < 0.001)

evidence.claim: Human oversight and system-level governance are explicitly referenced.
evidence.excerpt: recent risk frameworks and practitioner taxonomies emphasize prompt injection, insecure output handling, data leakage, and human oversight for LLM applications

evidence.claim: Work extends programmable guardrails from conversational applications to structured document generation.
evidence.excerpt: NeMo Guardrails shows how programmable rails can control conversational LLM applications through interpretable runtime policies [14]. Our work extends this direction to multimodal structured document generation

evidence.claim: Legacy production flow included manual triage and re-prompting after separate guardrail gates.
evidence.excerpt: an LLM produced a draft, then PII detection and content moderation were applied as separate services; failures triggered manual triage or re-prompting.

evidence.claim: Responsible-AI review identifies risks requiring human oversight.
evidence.excerpt: The Responsible-AI review decks also identify operational risks requiring human oversight, including title drift in generated evidence, analyzer/OCR failure, cropped text loss, UI bleed, and poor handwritten/blurry-image extraction.

evidence.claim: Transferability requires domain-specific recalibration including human-review policies.
evidence.excerpt: pattern may transfer to other structured document-generation settings, but rule weights, thresholds, risk routing, and human-review policies must be re-calibrated for each domain.
we document the reproducibility boundary through the request interface, scoring logic, pseudocode, and operational evidence boundary.

evidence.claim: Reviewer-calibrated Responsible-AI evidence-quality signals were collected.
evidence.excerpt: We also report reviewer-calibrated Responsible-AI evidence-quality signals from 770 generated-evidence reviews and a 70-case OCR slice
